source.title: Photon: Federated LLM Pre-Training
source.authors: Lorenzo Sani; Alexandru Iacob; Ze-Yu Cao; Royson Lee; Bill Marino; Yan Gao; Dong-Qi Cai; Ze-Xi Li; Wanru Zhao; Xin-Chi Qiu; N. Lane

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including appendices. It contains some OCR/flattening issues in tables and figures, but the relevant prose and Table 2 results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies federated LLM pre-training and reports validation perplexity, but it does not test memorization of random labels, the listed image-classification comparisons, or the specified generalization-gap measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports federated-versus-centralized validation perplexity and discusses generalization as an explanation. Those outcomes do not test any listed version: there is no random-label memorization test, interpolation-width sweep, architecture comparison, optimizer generalization comparison, dropout test, sharpness measure, or memorized-example removal.
record.test_reason: Photon uses the presumed generalization benefit of small local batches to motivate its training recipe (Sections 3 and C.1), but reports system and model performance without testing a supplied version. Batch-size experiments measure time to target perplexity; node-failure experiments measure training perplexity. Neither establishes held-out performance differences under fixed epoch budgets.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that Photon enables federated pre-training up to 7B parameters with lower reported validation perplexity than centralized training and lower communication costs. They attribute performance partly to small local batches, high learning rates, and federated optimization; the proposed generalization mechanisms are explanations rather than separately established results.
record.recipe_differences: Federated LLM pre-training using local AdamW updates and federated aggregation; the paper compares against centralized pre-training and DiLoCo, not the methods in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that outcomes vary with model size, global batch size, local steps per round, client participation, and data heterogeneity.

fits_no_version.finding: Photon's C4 validation perplexities are 20.1, 15.7, and 13.8 versus centralized baselines of 23.2, 18.2, and 16.6 at 1.3B, 3B, and 7B parameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The reported Photon training recipes achieve lower C4 validation perplexity than the reported centralized recipes at these model sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing the number of clients changes time to target validation perplexity, with diminishing returns depending on local steps and the target (Section 5.3, Figure 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Federated compute scaling has workload-dependent efficiency limits.

fits_no_version.finding: Moderate client dropout can improve final training perplexity at matched total tokens while requiring more rounds; dropout of seven of eight clients prevents convergence (Appendix D.2, Figures 11–12).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Client failures alter federated optimization and training efficiency, with extreme failure rates preventing convergence under the tested recipe.

record.code_released: The paper says the code is publicly available, but supplies no URL.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the Table 2 perplexity comparisons. This paper does not evaluate random-label memorization or any of the listed gap-related mechanisms.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on the listed versions were reported. The paper includes other system measurements, training perplexity curves, dropout experiments, and downstream task scores, but these do not measure the behaviors named by the versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out performance under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under comparable tuning. DiLoCo's server momentum comparison does not isolate this contrast; local training uses AdamW.
Held-out performance across batch sizes at fixed epoch or token budgets, including whether recipe adaptations remove a large-batch penalty.
Regularization dropout effects on held-out classifier error. The appendix's dropout experiments remove participating clients, not neural activations.
Measured magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures. Robust minima are invoked as an explanation without being measured.
Identifying memorized examples and comparing their removal with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T6 classification overlooks the explicit use of small-batch generalization findings to motivate Photon. Its declaration that all dropout experiments are irrelevant is correct for V6 because these are client failures. Additional experiments described under rows_left_out do not supply a test of the listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer held-out performance under the specified tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to train-test gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
